FOOTNOTES

1/ General Appropriations Act funds are appropriated as an Operating Lump Sum with Special Line Items by Agency.

Operating Budget

The Baseline includes \$6,537,200 and 64 FTE Positions from the Board of Nursing Fund in FY 2027 for the operating budget. These amounts are unchanged from FY 2026.

Certified Nursing Assistant Credentialing Program

The Baseline includes \$557,000 from the Board of Nursing Fund in FY 2027 for the Certified Nursing Assistant (CNA) Credentialing Program line item. This amount is unchanged from FY 2026.

The board registers CNAs at no charge to the individual and with no fingerprinting requirement. This policy meets federal requirements for having a nurse assistant (aide) registry.

Monies in this line item fund CNA Credentialing Program costs not paid by federal monies.

Student Registered Nurse Anesthetist Clinical Rotation Program

The Baseline includes no funding in FY 2027 for the Student Registered Nurse Anesthetist Clinical Rotation Program line item. Adjustments are as follows:

Remove One-Time Program Funding

The Baseline includes a one-time decrease of \$(500,000) from the General Fund in FY 2027 to remove grants to

health care institutions for student nurse anesthetist clinical training placements costs.

Healthcare Workforce Development Funding

The 3-year spending plan associated with the enacted FY 2023 budget assumed the Executive would spend \$27,000,000 in each of FY 2023, FY 2024, and FY 2025 from federal American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) State and Local Fiscal Recovery monies for the Student Nurse Clinical Rotation and Licensed or Certified Nurse Training Program established by Laws 2022, Chapter 330. The program provides grants to hospitals, nursing facilities, and assisted living facilities to expand or create clinical training placements for undergraduate nursing students and licensed or certified nurses. As of November 2025, the Board had spent \$4,650,700 in FY 2024, \$22,467,000 in FY 2025, and \$9,883,700 in the first 5 months of FY 2026.

AHCCCS designated the Arizona State Board of Nursing as the administrator of the program in December 2022 and transferred the ARPA monies to the Nursing Board. At its October 2, 2025, advisory meeting, the Board reported that 7,872 nurses have been trained as preceptors during the first two years of the program. Additionally, the Board stated that retention rates of preceptors increased by 8%- 10%, and 868 nurses received specialty or new clinal service education from the program.

In September 2025, the Auditor General published a performance audit and sunset review of the Arizona State Board of Nursing.

The Auditor General made 44 recommendations to the Board, most of which concerned proper complaint resolution. Only 1 recommendation had a budget implication.

Specifically, the Auditor General recommended the Board continue to assess its investigator-to-case ratios to determine if additional staff are needed to investigate complaints in a timely manner and reduce the existing backlog.

The Board agreed to implement all 44 recommendations.
